categories.name: Atelier notes
categories.description: News from the room in Kagurazaka.

posts.title: A slower evening routine
posts.excerpt: Oil first, then water, then nothing for a minute. Mio on why the pause matters more than the product.
posts.content:
Most of us rush the evening. We wipe, splash and pat, and wonder why skin feels tight by morning.

Oil on dry skin

Start with Camellia Cleansing Oil on dry hands and a dry face. Massage for a full minute; this is where the day comes off.

Then add a little warm water, let the oil turn milky, and rinse.

Then pause

Before toner, wait a moment. Let the skin settle. It is the cheapest step in any routine and the one we skip most.

posts.title: Why we steep yuzu peel
posts.excerpt: The peel left over from juice pressing in Kochi becomes the heart of our serum. Ren explains the slow steep.
posts.content:
Every winter a grower in Kochi presses yuzu for juice and sends us the peel.

Six weeks in rice alcohol

We steep the peel cold for six weeks, then filter it twice. The result is pale gold and smells exactly like the fruit.

That extract is about four percent of the Yuzu Clarity Serum, and all of its scent.

posts.title: Rice ferment from a sake brewer
posts.excerpt: A small brewer in Niigata keeps back the clear liquid after pressing. It is why our cream feels the way it does.
posts.content:
Brewers have known about soft hands for centuries. The liquid left after pressing sake rice is mild, slightly acidic and full of the good things fermentation leaves behind.

From the brewery to the jar

We collect it twice a year, filter it and blend it into Rice Milk Cream within the week.

posts.title: Green tea, cold steeped
posts.excerpt: First-flush leaves from Shizuoka, steeped cold for a day. The toner that calms everything down.
posts.content:
Hot water draws out bitterness. Cold water, slowly, keeps the calm.

A day in the fridge

We steep first-flush leaves in cold water for twenty-four hours, filter twice and bottle the toner the same afternoon.

posts.title: A routine for sensitive skin
posts.excerpt: Three products, nothing new for two weeks, and a patch test first. Hana on starting gently.
posts.content:
When skin is unhappy, the kindest thing is often to do less.

Three steps only

Camellia Cleansing Oil in the evening, Green Tea Toner morning and night, Rice Milk Cream to finish. Nothing else for two weeks.

Patch test anything new behind the ear first, for two evenings.

posts.title: Refills at the atelier
posts.excerpt: Bring any of our bottles back and we refill it while you wait, for less than a new one.
posts.content:
Glass is lovely to hold and easy to wash. It seemed wrong to throw it away.

How refills work

Bring a clean bottle to the atelier. We refill serums, toners, mists and oils at the counter while you wait, for about a fifth less than a new bottle.

Empty jars and bottles you no longer need can come back too; we clean and reuse them.
